why: The I-PACE model explains the development and maintenance of addictive online behaviors through person–affect–cognition–execution processes, not how people learn or are taught.
The candidate is the productive-failure/PS-I account, a narrower instructional-sequencing case already covered by Problem-Solving Followed by Instruction.

claims.verifier: The claim directly tests problem-solving followed by instruction against instruction-first sequencing and reports the predicted advantage.
Directly tests PS-I versus instruction-first and provides a relevant boundary-condition result favoring instruction-first for higher-prior-knowledge students.
It directly qualifies PS-I by showing that prior knowledge alone may not determine which instructional sequence is optimal.

why: I-SEE is an online implementation of self-regulated learning that scaffolds learners' planning, monitoring, assessment and adjustment through recursive resources, guidance, activities and feedback.
The I-AIM framework is a domain-specific competency and assessment framework for point-of-care ultrasound training, not a general explanatory theory of learning.
name: I-AIM framework for organizing and assessing PoCUS competency
product_description: A clinical education framework used by PoCUS educators to organize competency development and assessment across indication, image acquisition, interpretation, and medical decision-making.

why: I Control is a named, structured yearlong curriculum package combining scripted self-regulation lessons with computerized executive-function games, rather than a general instructional element.
name: I Control
product_description: I Control is a yearlong self-regulation curriculum developed for middle-school students with significant emotional and behavioral problems, combining scripted classroom lessons with the Brain Training Lab computerized executive-function games.

why: The I-ACT is a named standardized assessment instrument, not a general instructional element; its scoring approach is an instance of assessment and rubric use.
name: I-ACT (Interprofessional Anschutz Communication Skills Toolbox) standardized patient assessment instrument
product_description: A CAPE-established 15-question instrument used by trained standardized patients to assess healthcare students' communication performance in simulated clinical encounters.
